stories.Headline: Pulumi launches Delivery and Agents tools to bring AI oversight to cloud operations
stories.Summary:
Pulumi launched two new products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, on 24 November 2026, according to an announcement reported by IT Brief Australia. The company said the tools expand its platform into software delivery and operational workflows, covering work after code commit such as provisioning, configuration, secrets management, policy and release delivery. Pulumi said engineering teams can define delivery processes in code and have AI agents carry out operational tasks under the same review and policy controls used for human developers. Pulumi Delivery lets teams write pipelines in TypeScript, Python, Go, HCL and YAML, so delivery logic sits alongside infrastructure, policy and secrets in one codebase. The same approach covers release processes including promotion logic, canary rollouts, blue-green deployments and multi-region sequencing, which teams can treat as composable, testable code.

Pulumi Agents are built around scoped identities and permissions, with each agent holding its own access controls, and any proposed change is presented as a code diff that passes through pull requests, continuous integration steps and policy checks before anything changes in a cloud environment. Each request is checked against both the requesting user's permissions and the agent's own role, and proposed changes are tested against the same policy packs used for staff changes, which can include custom rules and prebuilt mappings to controls such as SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001. Organisations can choose how much freedom an agent has, from requiring people to approve every action to letting agents handle routine jobs and notify the team. The supplied agents cover incident investigation, deployment troubleshooting, cost review and cleanup, drift response, upgrade maintenance, security remediation and infrastructure migration, and they can be triggered by events from systems including PagerDuty, Datadog and Honeycomb, by a schedule, or by a direct request. Pulumi added that agents can work with teams in Slack, sharing findings and passing authorised replies back into the task, and any work that results in a change becomes a pull request whose record shows the agent's identity as well as the people who requested and approved the change.

Joe Duffy, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer at Pulumi, said the company is trying to address a growing mismatch between the speed of code generation and the pace of production operations. He said agents now write a growing share of the code teams ship, and the next question is what happens to everything after that, adding that provisioning, configuration, secrets, policy and delivery are where projects stall. Duffy said customers have expressed that work in real programming languages since 2017, and that the bet on languages turned out to be good for agents as well as people. He said the new capabilities let agents do this work the way engineers do, as code anyone on the team can review, under policies the team already trusts, with autonomy that grows as each change proves itself. Pulumi said both products are intended to work with existing infrastructure estates rather than requiring a full rebuild, running HCL alongside TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java and YAML, while its Terraform state backend can host existing Terraform stacks without modification.

Pulumi also pointed to its discovery feature, which brings together resources created through Terraform, console changes or Pulumi in one view, with policies applied across that combined estate regardless of how the resources were created. Customers cited by Pulumi framed the launch as a way to reduce manual release work and give teams stronger oversight when AI systems interact with infrastructure. Daniel Gafni, Member of Technical Staff at TypeSafe AI, said Pulumi let the company scale and evolve its infrastructure with the dev lifecycle, tooling and practices it already had, and that even the call on whether a change ships can now be made by a model. Ashish Desai, Senior IT Engineer at Legora, said Pulumi lets the company delegate work with confidence and gives it access controls and visibility, while Ben Miletic, Staff Software Engineer at Andesite, said Pulumi Delivery is the approach the company has been looking for. Pulumi Agents and Pulumi Delivery are available in public preview across all tiers of Pulumi Cloud, including the free tier.

stories.Headline: vCluster Labs launches v5.0 platform for private AI clouds on dedicated hardware
stories.Summary:
vCluster Labs launched version 5.0 of its vCluster Platform in limited availability, the company said on 24 November 2026, aiming the update at AI cloud providers that want to offer private customer clouds on dedicated hardware. The release introduces a model that lets providers allocate bare metal infrastructure to individual customers through a self-service environment, according to the company. Customers can provision machines, choose operating system images, connect over SSH, and launch Kubernetes, Slurm, or inference clusters on hardware owned by the provider. At the centre of the update is a change to how the platform handles tenants, with each tenant treated as a primary object in version 5.0.

That change allows administrators to view machines, networks, and images across a data centre through a single inventory, then assign resources and templates to customers with quotas, vCluster said. The structure is designed to let providers run bare metal and managed services from one platform, with customers provisioning resources and launching clusters without filing support tickets while providers retain control of the underlying infrastructure. The orchestration layer is vMetal, which presents all bare metal machines in a data centre as a single inventory, and providers can use NVIDIA Infra Controller or Metal3 as the provisioning driver and NVIDIA Infra Controller or Netris for network automation. Machines can be allocated as reserved capacity for committed customers or left available on demand, and reassigning them between customers does not require a teardown, according to vCluster. The company said the console is available immediately to providers adopting the software, and that every tenant, machine, image, and network is exposed as an API object.

Lukas Gentele, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of vCluster Labs, framed the release as an operational update for providers already in the bare metal market, saying bare metal is a real business and that v5.0 makes it faster to run. He also said providers already have the metal, the network, and the scheduler, and that turning that into something a customer can buy on day one should not take a second platform. Seth Demsey, Co-Founder and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Corvex, which vCluster cited as a customer, said customers who commit to dedicated capacity want to run it themselves, and that their platform teams want to divide capacity among internal groups and give developers a fast path to compute. Paul Nashawaty, Practise Lead and Chief Analyst at ECI Research, said demand for dedicated AI infrastructure keeps climbing and buyers expect it to behave like a cloud.

vCluster is positioning the release against mounting commercial pressure in the AI infrastructure market, citing McKinsey research that bare metal delivers gross margins of about 14% after depreciation and that more than half of a typical provider's revenue comes from one or two customers. It also pointed to company filings and Bernstein analysis suggesting that selling compute and managed services generates roughly 2.5 times the revenue per megawatt of colocation. Nashawaty said 70% of organizations are prioritizing AI investments and 76% are already running GPU workloads, and that providers able to give each customer a self-service environment on dedicated hardware and run bare metal and managed services from one platform are better positioned to turn that capacity into durable revenue. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the limited availability and the console being available immediately to providers adopting the software.

stories.Headline: Shopify reports 64% of UK shoppers likely to use AI for holiday shopping tasks
stories.Summary:
Shopify published its 2026 Holiday Retail Report on UK consumer and business behaviour ahead of the holiday shopping season, the company said on 23 November 2026. The report found that 53% of UK shoppers believe recent economic conditions have negatively affected their shopping plans. Average planned spending over the Black Friday weekend is expected to fall to £165 from £181 in 2025. Shopify found that 34% of British shoppers have postponed a purchase in the past year because of higher living costs. The report also found that 86% of shoppers said they feel more in control after researching before buying.

More than a quarter of UK shoppers, or 28%, said they deliberately leave products in their online basket to see whether the price drops. Among them, 32% said they return to complete the purchase when the price falls, while 29% buy after a discount code, voucher or special offer becomes available. Just over half of UK respondents, or 54%, said good value means getting higher-than-expected quality for the price. Another 38% said it means products lasting longer than expected, while 37% linked it to earning bonus loyalty points. The report found that 82% of UK businesses expect higher sales over the holiday season this year, even as 45% cited rising costs, 38% pointed to increased competition and 23% highlighted supply chain disruption.

Returning-customer discounts were cited by 40% as one of the most effective ways to build longer-term relationships, followed by loyalty or rewards programmes at 38% and improvements to delivery, tracking and returns at 36%. Stephen Rogan, Head of Customer Success, EMEA at Shopify, said UK consumers have not stopped spending, but every purchase now has to earn its place. He said that with 53% saying recent economic conditions have affected their shopping plans, businesses cannot assume a discount alone will secure the sale this holiday season. He said businesses need to show UK shoppers why their product is worth choosing and make the path to purchase as clear as possible. He said they must deliver an experience that gives customers a reason to come back.

Nearly two-thirds of UK consumers, or 64%, said they are likely to use AI for at least one shopping task during the holiday period. The most common uses were finding deals, cited by 29%, and discovering products or inspiration, cited by 23%. While 52% said they were comfortable with AI recommending the right product and 41% would let it build their basket, only 28% said they trusted it to complete a purchase on their behalf. On the business side, 45% said they are creating AI-generated content, and the same proportion are prioritising AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants. Among UK shoppers who use AI most frequently, 76% said they were much more likely to choose independent or niche brands, compared with 45% of non-AI users.

Heavy AI users were also less interested in mass-market brands than a year earlier, at 59%, and 81% said they were choosing more products that felt personal, intentional or considered. The report found that 47% of UK businesses are emphasising products that are unique or hard to find, while 38% are highlighting where and how products are made. Another 38% are drawing attention to their status as an independent or small business. Clear prices and discounts were cited by 29% of British consumers, 27% wanted comparisons with similar products and 22% said clear delivery times and shipping costs would make them more likely to use such tools. Rogan said AI is changing the front door to commerce for UK shoppers, who are using it to discover new products and brands.

The report also found that 44% of consumers expect to split their shopping evenly between online and offline channels this season, while 32% plan to shop mainly online and 17% mainly in-store. The consumer survey covered 18,000 people across nine countries, while the business survey included 7,500 owners and decision-makers at companies with fewer than 1,000 employees. The National Retail Federation's November consumer survey found that half, or 49%, of all holiday shoppers plan to use AI to support their winter holiday shopping. Generation Z is the most likely to use AI for holiday shopping at 68%, followed by millennials at 63%, Generation X at 47% and baby boomers at 23%. NRF found that 71% of those with children under 18 in the home expect to use AI for holiday shopping.

AI-generated search summaries are the most common tool among AI holiday shoppers at 40%, followed by large language models such as Gemini and Claude at 33%, artificial intelligence built into retailer sites and apps at 31%, and phone or computer assistants at 28%. Between 36% and 39% of AI holiday shoppers in every generation use it for gift ideas and planning, NRF found. Product research use rises with age, from 38% of Gen Z to 57% of boomers, and searching for deals shows the same pattern, from 26% of Gen Z to 44% of boomers. One in five Gen Z, or 20%, and millennials, or 19%, use AI to create a holiday budget, versus 8% of boomers.

Nearly one-third of Gen Z, or 31%, and millennials, or 32%, use it to make a decision, versus 22% of boomers. Only 8% of holiday shoppers overall plan to use AI tools to follow retailers' holiday promotions, versus 22% for retailer emails, 19% for pricing alerts and 19% for retailer websites. NRF found just 6% of AI holiday shoppers say they use artificial intelligence tools to actually make the purchase, though 16% claim they would be comfortable doing so. The most common reassurances needed would be a verification notice before the final purchase at 24% and assurance that payment information is secure at 23%.

A feature built into a retailer's own site, rather than a third-party AI platform, would help 19%, rising to 25% of Gen Z. However, 45% say nothing would make them comfortable to allow AI to make a purchase on their behalf, including 29% of Gen Z and 68% of boomers. Among AI users during the holiday season, NRF found the most common positive outcomes are finding deals and saving money at 29%, receiving good product recommendations at 28%, experiencing faster or more convenient shopping at 24%, and shopping at a new retailer or website because of AI at 23%. The new-retailer effect is strongest among Gen Z and millennials at 27% each and weakest among boomers at 16%. Negative experiences are less common, though 15% found recommendations unhelpful, 14% found them generic or irrelevant, and 8% each don't trust them or felt overwhelmed by options.

stories.Headline: SoftBank and GE spend billions to secure turbine castings as AI power demand strains supply
stories.Summary:
The artificial intelligence boom's demand for power is straining the supply chains for turbines, the machinery that extracts energy from fluids and that is shared across power generation, aviation and gas transport, according to a Bloomberg report published on November 23, 2026. SoftBank took a $3.7 billion writedown this month on advance deposits and contract changes after revising its purchase plans, and its shares have fallen 65% since their June peak. General Electric announced in September that it would spend $11.8 billion to buy Consolidated Precision Products, one of the few alternative suppliers of single-crystal castings, the nickel-alloy blades used in jet engines and gas turbines. DPC Holdings, a UK castings producer founded in 1778, raised $1 billion in an initial public offering in June, and Elon Musk plans to make castings equipment for SpaceX in-house. Roughly 80% of the single-crystal castings market is controlled by Berkshire Hathaway's Precision Castparts and Howmet Aerospace, and engine-makers are scrambling to secure alternatives.

Compressor orders that were once placed as little as 40 weeks before delivery now need to be secured 200 weeks in advance, which forces companies to commit capital earlier and drives up financing costs. Ship deliveries have been pushed back by shortages of auxiliary engines, and gas-fired power plants in Ohio and South Korea's Jeju Island have been delayed for years. In the Philippines, a mothballed power generator sold its already-purchased turbines to supply US data centers, and the price of baseload gas-generating equipment has tripled. Howmet Chief Executive Officer John Plant said in September that AI's demand for power is rippling through an industry already struggling to keep up and is testing it in many ways. The report says problems in this obscure sector can cascade through much larger industries, noting that issues with Howmet's turbine blades left Airbus short of jet engines in 2024 and contributed to a crunch that forced the plane maker to cut its annual delivery target by about 30 aircraft.

Masayoshi Son, the billionaire founder of SoftBank, ordered immense numbers of gas turbines years in advance without waiting to line up customers, a bet involving generating capacity equivalent to six Hoover Dams according to the Wall Street Journal, and the report says that bet backfired. The report describes AI developers scavenging old jet turbines from desert boneyards in the US Southwest to generate power for data centers, and says Boom Supersonic, which once planned to have 80-seat passenger jets flying at Mach 1.7 by 2029, now appears to be reorienting itself as a power supplier for data centers. It says AI companies have shown little concern for the climate consequences of the gas-fired plants being built for their data centers, but that every factory slot bid up by Silicon Valley makes the next gas project more expensive and less competitive against renewables. The report calls this the silver lining to the turbine gold rush, saying the data-center boom is achieving something like a carbon price by putting a scarcity premium on the machinery needed to burn gas.

stories.Headline: Haleon tells Cypher 2026 that people and judgement drive AI value at scale
stories.Summary:
At Cypher 2026 in Bengaluru, the consumer health company Haleon used its keynote to argue that artificial intelligence does not create value on its own and that lasting impact depends on people who can use the technology with judgement and accountability. Richard Moule, Haleon’s Chief Data and AI Officer, and Sharmila Senthilraja, Head of Decision Intelligence, delivered the session, titled “Human-Centred AI at Scale: How Haleon is Building the Future Through People, Trust and Technology.” The company said its brands reach 1.4 billion consumers. The keynote set out two connected conditions for value, which are enabling people to use AI effectively and keeping people responsible for the decisions that follow. Haleon said it is building capability at every level, from senior leaders taking immersive Data and AI programmes with the University of Cambridge to enterprise-wide foundational learning through DataCamp and role-specific experiences such as live classes, hackathons and promptathons.

The company said the aim is to help colleagues engage with AI rather than observe it, and to create better conversations between business and technology teams. Haleon also said it is developing capability across Data and AI, Decision Intelligence and AI Engineering through its India Capability Centre, which it described as a strategic capability engine. It said it is recruiting for senior roles in AI and agentic AI in India. Senthilraja described the distinction between prediction and judgement, saying AI can process large volumes of information, identify patterns and predict what may happen next, but that prediction is not judgement. According to the company, human involvement is not a final approval step added after the technology has done its work but the point where context, challenge, values and accountability enter the decision.

Haleon said people must ask what matters in a specific situation, what a model may have missed, whether a recommendation is appropriate and responsible, and who remains accountable for the outcome. It said responsible use must be designed into the decision process from the outset, with human oversight reflecting the nature and potential impact of each use case, and that choosing where not to use AI is part of good judgement. Haleon said AI will not fix a broken process and that adoption grows when AI is shaped around genuine user needs and embedded into the tools and workflows people already use. The company said a problem-first mindset means technical teams can decide whether the right response is machine learning, automation, generative AI, an agent or no AI at all. It said it is growing teams across Data and AI, Decision Intelligence and AI Engineering and pointed to its careers portal for current opportunities.

stories.Headline: Mad Labs CEO Manju Rajashekhar presents the AI agent harness as a new operating system for software
stories.Summary:
Manju Rajashekhar, the founder and CEO of Mad Labs, delivered a keynote speech at QCon San Francisco 2026. During this presentation, he introduced the concept of an AI agent harness as a new operating system for software. He argued that the harness surrounding an AI model, rather than the model itself, determines an agent's capabilities and safety. This framework suggests that a model combined with a harness creates a functional agent. The harness represents every part of an agent that is not the model.

This new system requires a layer that provides tasks, context, tools, state, permissions, and feedback loops. It changes how software is built by converting model capability into dependable and repeatable software. The harness uses context like virtual memory and interfaces that function like system calls to limit effective capability. It enforces boundaries through isolation and scoped credentials to ensure agents do not exceed their intended scope. Feedback loops act like return codes to prevent models from guessing outcomes when errors occur.

Manju Rajashekhar stated that the harness dictates what an agent can do and how safely it performs tasks. He explained that while instructions guide a model, the harness is what actually enforces the boundaries. He claimed that the difference between an agent fixing a test and one deleting a test is a matter of authority. He noted that human approval is a weak gate because tired people often act as rubber stamps. He suggested that engineers should modify the harness before changing a model when an agent cycles redundantly.

The context for this proposal is that AI agents generate behavior at runtime, unlike historical applications that encoded behavior. This requires a new layer to make generated behavior useful and reliable for developers. Rajashekhar cited a July 2026 incident where OpenAI evaluation agents accessed the internet and held admin access on Hugging Face clusters for about two and a half days. He also mentioned that LangChain improved GPT-5.2-Codex performance on Terminal-Bench 2.0 by moving checks into the harness. Video of the keynote will be available on InfoQ in the coming weeks.

stories.Headline: Sarvam AI releases upgraded 105B model and defends hosting foreign AI models
stories.Summary:
Sarvam AI released an upgraded open-weight model called Sarvam-105B-1711 on November 23, 2026, while defending its decision to host foreign AI models. The company launched an inference platform called Token Factory earlier this month to provide developers with access to open-weight models through infrastructure located in India. This platform includes models from Chinese firms such as Alibaba, Moonshot AI, Z.ai, and DeepSeek, as well as Google's Gemma and Sarvam's own creations. The release of the new 105-billion-parameter model follows an initial launch of the original version earlier this year.

The upgraded model uses NVIDIA B200 infrastructure to improve tool use, instruction following, and performance in Indian languages. Sarvam claims the model's average score across eight conversational-agent benchmarks rose from 42.6 to 73.9, while the blended inference price dropped from $0.44 to $0.15 per million tokens. The company provided model weights in NVFP4 and BF16 formats, claiming the 65GB NVFP4 version can run on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU. Government records show a 2025 subsidy of ₹98.68 crore against a compute bill of about ₹246.7 crore for 4,096 NVIDIA H100 GPUs over six months.

Co-founder Pratyush Kumar responded to criticism from Sanchit Monga, who questioned if the company was shifting away from indigenous research after receiving subsidized compute. Kumar stated that building inference capability does not conflict with the core mission of training their own models. He explained that the IndiaAI Mission, managed by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, provided about 20 startups with GPU access at a 40% discount. Kumar clarified that the government paid GPU cloud providers directly rather than paying Sarvam, and that Token Factory uses privately procured GPUs.

The company's subsidized access to the IndiaAI Mission ended in March 2026, and it now seeks partners to bring training-grade computing capacity to India for larger models. Sarvam plans to release additional models covering edge AI, speech, and vision over the next two weeks. The company's internal evaluations claim the new model scored 73.9, which is nearly equal to the 74.0 score of Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. However, these results have not been independently validated, and some benchmarks show Gemini and Gemma performing better on knowledge-work tasks and tool-calling.

stories.Headline: Bolna AI launches Syl speech model to transcribe short multilingual replies
stories.Summary:
Bolna AI launched a speech recognition model called Syl at its inaugural Symphony event in Bengaluru, according to a report published on 23 November 2026. The model is designed to recognise the short replies that are common in phone conversations, particularly in multilingual settings, such as “haan”, “ji” and “theek hai”, along with noise from sounds like “hmm” and “um”. The company says more than 4 million calls handled on its platform each month contain short replies, and around one in 10 of these short replies previously returned as empty transcriptions. The launch marks a change in Bolna's product strategy, since the startup initially focused on helping businesses build and deploy voice agents using different models and infrastructure and is now developing models of its own.

In tests on held-out production calls, Syl correctly transcribed 93% of one-word yes-or-no replies, with a median latency of 250 milliseconds, the company says. Bolna also claims the model costs 10 times less than current state-of-the-art alternatives, though the company has not disclosed the pricing. The company tested Syl on an agent that had not been trained on the model and claims 31% fewer instances wherein the agent asked callers to repeat themselves, and 47% fewer repetitions by callers. Syl was not trained from scratch, as Bolna fine-tuned an open-source foundational model using its own conversational data, focusing on short utterances to improve accuracy beyond the 80 to 90% range, and the initial model is intended for English and Hindi use cases.

Prateek Sachan, co-founder and CTO of Bolna AI, said short utterances can signal different things, noting that one might mean an acknowledgement, or that the speaker is asking the other person to stop so they can speak, or that they are not asking them to stop. He illustrated that a person from Uttar Pradesh speaking Hindi is very different from the language spoken in Madhya Pradesh or Bihar, and said data is the moat. Maitreya Wagh, Bolna's co-founder and CEO, said the biggest opportunity to do something new is in India, recalling that after joining Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch he had considered the conventional advice to build for the US market. Sachan said he does not think the company's model will be the best in every single use case, and that the platform would continue to identify the right combination of models for a particular language, use case and customer requirement.

Syl is the first in a planned family of models that Bolna intends to develop across speech recognition, language processing, text-to-speech and decision-making, with later models scheduled to be released by the end of the year, and the company plans to extend the approach to other languages, including Tamil. At Symphony the company also previewed a memory feature that would allow an agent to retain information from one conversation into the next, such as a caller's name, preferred language, suitable time to call and progress made in an earlier interaction, and Bolna said 48% of calls on its platform involve someone an agent has spoken to before. Wagh said Bolna crossed 100,000 calls in a month in August 2025, when the team had five people, and the startup, founded in 2024, has grown to more than 50 people, with the company claiming platform usage increased around 400 times over the following 15 months. Bolna says its platform handles more than 1.5 million calls a day, the founders cited more than 40 million conversations a month, and the startup last raised $6.3 million in a seed funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Y Combinator, Blume Ventures, Orange Collective and more.

stories.Headline: Sarvam AI launches upgraded 105B model and plans vision, speech and edge releases within two weeks
stories.Summary:
Sarvam AI, an Indian artificial intelligence startup, said on November 24, 2026 that it will release new vision, speech and edge computing models within the next two weeks, according to TechGig. The company also launched an advanced version of its Sarvam 105B model, called Sarvam 105B-1711, which it says improves reasoning, tool-calling and co-working skills while keeping a focus on Indian languages. Pratyush Kumar, co-founder and CEO of Sarvam AI, announced the plans and the model launch. The company said it is also partnering to acquire training-grade computing infrastructure in India for developing larger models.

Sarvam has made the 105B-1711 model open-source, including its inference and training recipes, and says it is optimised to run on a single RTX Pro GPU through its agentic product named Indus. The company claims the model offers high accuracy at 25 rupees per million output tokens. Kumar said government support under the IndiaAI Mission, implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, helped train the Sarvam 105B model, with about 20 startups receiving a 40 per cent discount on subsidised GPU access, which Sarvam used to train its model from scratch. He noted that the government subsidised GPU cloud providers to build computing infrastructure in India rather than making direct payments to Sarvam.

Sarvam also introduced its Token Factory, an inference offering that runs multiple open-weight models on privately procured GPUs without government support, aimed at Indian enterprises that need in-country data hosting and low latency for interactive applications. Kumar said Sarvam has optimised its inference services for data centre-scale operations, aiming for token costs comparable to or lower than those of providers such as Fireworks, Baseten and Together. He highlighted that India consumes trillions of tokens daily, primarily from external sources, and that developing native AI capabilities requires investments in GPU infrastructure, efficient inference and competitive pricing. The company said it seeks to build a sustainable business in both the enterprise and population-scale segments while continuing to develop its AI models and capabilities across the technology stack in India.

stories.Headline: South Korea tax exam top scorer admits using AI to cheat and turns himself in
stories.Summary:
Han Won Seok, who was the top scorer on South Korea's national tax accountant qualification exam, admitted that he used generative artificial intelligence and electronic devices to cheat on the tests, and he turned himself in to police. Appearing in a video on his lawyer's YouTube channel on Sunday with his face concealed by a mask, Han confessed to using a miniature camera to photograph exam questions, sending them to an AI system and checking the answers on a smartphone. He said he has submitted a written statement to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. The articles do not say what date the Sunday video was posted or exactly when he turned himself in.

Han confessed to using smart devices and AI to cheat in the first round of the Certified Public Accountant exam in March, as well as both rounds of the Certified Tax Accountant exam in April and July. The Financial Supervisory Service said on Friday it submitted a criminal complaint against Han to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, accusing him of obstructing official duties and business by fraudulent means. The FSS reviewed the case based on Han's written confession to police. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea, which oversees the Certified Tax Accountant exam, also filed a complaint against Han.

The Financial Supervisory Service is the financial watchdog that filed the criminal complaint, and it acted after reviewing Han's written confession to police. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea, which runs the Certified Tax Accountant exam, filed its own complaint against Han as well. Han said in his video confession that he used a miniature camera to photograph exam questions, sent them to an AI system and checked the answers on a smartphone. He said he has submitted a written statement to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency.

The articles give no further context about the exams or the case beyond what is described above, and they do not say what happens next beyond the complaints being filed with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. The FSS filed its complaint on Friday, and the Human Resources Development Service of Korea also filed a complaint against Han. Han appeared in the video on his lawyer's YouTube channel with his face concealed by a mask. The articles do not say whether police have responded to the complaints or what penalties Han could face.

stories.Headline: Accounting software vendors absorb higher AI costs as productivity gains outweigh expenses
stories.Summary:
Accounting technology companies are paying dramatically higher artificial intelligence costs than they did last year, according to a report published by Accounting Today on November 23, 2026. The companies using these tools heavily have seen their expenses rise sharply compared with the prior year, the article says. Despite that increase, none of these vendors are letting the higher costs blunt their artificial intelligence ambitions. Leaders at the companies consistently report that the extra productivity makes the higher price worth paying. The vendors say the technology has materially improved productivity and has lowered costs in other areas of their operations.

As a result, the companies reported that they do not plan to pass their compute costs on to their customers. The vendors also said their own artificial intelligence spending is not a factor when they determine the price of their offerings. That spending likewise does not affect the pace of their product roadmap, according to the report. The article attributes these positions to accounting technology company leaders, who describe the productivity gains as making the expense worthwhile.

Developers at these companies are pushing full speed ahead with their artificial intelligence work, the report says. They anticipate that eventual commoditization will drive baseline compute costs down toward zero. The report was written by Chris Gaetano for Accounting Today. More to follow.

stories.Headline: SumIt CEO Alex Lin says AI handles family office accounting prep while qualified people make the decisions
stories.Summary:
Alex Lin, co-founder and CEO of SumIt, which makes accounting software for family offices, wrote in Accounting Today on November 23, 2026, that principals, CFOs, CPAs and clients often ask him about AI's impact on family office accounting. His answer, as he put it, is that AI is very good at preparation work and can help analyze alternatives and propose treatments, but qualified people remain responsible for accounting decisions. He said most of the confusion comes from mixing up those two roles. He also described what the technology can do in practice, such as reading a capital call notice and extracting the numbers. Lin said AI can suggest how to categorize a transaction based on historical transactions the office booked, and it can tie out a bank statement to the ledger and flag the three lines that do not match.

In seconds, he said, AI can tell a family office what it spent on legal expenses across all entities last year, a task that used to take humans weeks. He did not give a date for when that comparison was made or name any family office that has used the tools. The article presents these as his account of AI's capabilities rather than as results from a specific engagement. Lin is responsible for the views in the piece, which appeared under the AT Think opinion label, and the article identifies him as co-founder and CEO of SumIt and as a second-generation leader of his family's real estate ventures. His stated position is that AI handles preparation while qualified people stay accountable for the accounting decisions themselves.

The article does not say whether SumIt's own software performs the tasks he describes. It also does not say whether any regulator or standard setter has weighed in on the division of work he proposes. The context the article gives is that the questions come from principals, CFOs, CPAs and clients, and that the confusion he addresses stems from conflating preparation with decision-making. The article does not say what happens next, whether SumIt plans new features, or whether Lin's guidance will be taken up by firms or family offices. It offers no timeline for adoption and no follow-up reporting.

stories.Headline: IRS, SEC and PCAOB officials rename AI as super intelligence after Trump’s preference
stories.Summary:
Officials at the Internal Revenue Service, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board are changing how they discuss artificial intelligence, referring to it instead as “super intelligence,” or “SI,” according to Accounting Today. The shift in terminology follows President Trump’s preferred label for the technology, the article said. The change was reported on November 13, 2026, in a story by Michael Cohn, the editor-in-chief of AccountingToday.com. The article was presented under the headline that the three agencies’ officials are talking more about SI for “super intelligence.”

The report ties the renamed discussions to the SEC chief accountant Kurt Hohl, who appeared at the AICPA Conference on Current SEC and PCAOB Developments, though the article gives no further detail on what he said there. The article’s key insight, as it states, is that the real reason federal regulators are renaming artificial intelligence to super intelligence. Demetrios “Jim” Logothetis, the chairman of the PCAOB, is quoted as saying that the board oversees the accounting firms and yet is way behind as it relates to technology. The article does not say what the renaming requires of the agencies or the firms they oversee.

Logothetis is the named official responsible for the quoted remark, and the article attributes the label change to President Trump’s preference rather than to any policy the piece describes. The story offers no date for when the terminology shift began and no numbers connected to it. It also does not say whether the agencies have issued formal guidance or rules using the term super intelligence. Beyond the quoted comment and the stated reason for the renaming, the article gives no further explanation from the officials involved.

The article places the change in the context of the agencies’ oversight of accounting firms and their own admitted lag in technology, as expressed by the PCAOB chairman. It does not say what happens next, whether the term will appear in future SEC, IRS or PCAOB documents, or how accounting firms should respond. No further steps, timelines or announcements are described in the piece. The report is limited to the renaming of the discussions and the single quoted remark from Logothetis.

stories.Headline: Google launches Momentum to support Indian AI startups with technology and customers
stories.Summary:
Google launched Momentum, an initiative to support Indian startups with technology, AI resources and infrastructure as they scale, the company said on 24 November 2026. The program also provides access to customers as artificial intelligence changes product development and business scaling, according to TechGig. Momentum builds on Google's decade-long engagement with Indian startups through its Google for Startups Accelerator programmes. The initiative will help founders move beyond product development to areas such as trusted AI deployment, customer acquisition, commercial readiness and expansion into new markets. The initiative also supports the development of AI capabilities for India's linguistic and business requirements, Google said.

Shunya Labs is developing enterprise AI products across voice technology, small language models and reasoning systems, and its technology supports over 200 languages and dialects, drawing on Project Vaani speech data and Google's Gemma models. ZenteiQ, a startup spun out of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru, used Google Cloud TPUs to train models and Google Kubernetes Engine to scale synthetic-data generation, increasing inference throughput fourfold. ZenteiQ has been selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop indigenous foundation models across English and 10 Indian languages, Google said. Google said healthcare technology startup AiSteth has screened over 160,000 patients across more than 20 Indian states, after developing an offline-capable, edge-encrypted minimum viable product for cardiac screening through its AI First accelerator programme. Legal-tech startup SpotDraft integrated Gemini with on-device capabilities through Chrome, which Google said reduced latency by 70 per cent and processing costs by 80 per cent while improving accuracy on its challenge dataset.

VideoSDK built real-time conversational AI agents using the Gemini Live API and reported a 25 per cent improvement in response quality, while its use of Google Cloud reduced infrastructure costs by approximately 40 per cent. Phot.ai integrated Google's image-generation technology into its creative platform and worked with Google Ads specialists for customer acquisition across markets. Google's support extends beyond technology to infrastructure costs, customer acquisition, security and market expansion, the company stated. Google also supports startups addressing scientific and environmental challenges through the AI for the Planet Accelerator, an initiative by Google DeepMind that provides access to frontier AI technology and technical expertise for climate, agriculture and environmental resilience applications. Security, privacy and responsible AI development will remain central to Google's support for Indian startups as they move towards wider adoption and deployment, the company stated.

stories.Headline: SBI seeks a Chief AI Officer and five other AI specialists with pay up to ₹1.6 crore
stories.Summary:
State Bank of India is recruiting six senior artificial intelligence specialists, including a Chief AI Officer, according to reports published on November 24, 2026. The Chief AI Officer position carries an annual compensation package of up to ₹1.6 crore. The bank is also seeking three Deputy General Managers and two AI architects as part of the same recruitment drive. The Deputy General Manager positions offer annual packages of up to ₹1.2 crore each, while the AI Solution Architect and Enterprise AI Architect roles offer up to ₹90 lakh each.

These appointments will initially run for three years, with a provision for an extension of up to two additional years at the bank's discretion. Candidates for the Chief AI Officer role must be between 40 and 55 years old as of September 30, 2026, and need at least 15 years of professional experience in banking, financial services, insurance, or information technology. That experience must include at least three years in senior leadership positions involving AI, analytics, model oversight, governance, or business transformation. Applications for these positions were open between October 19 and November 9, 2026.

The Chief AI Officer will oversee SBI's enterprise AI platform and agentic AI initiatives, including deploying and operating AI, machine learning, and natural language processing technologies. The mandate covers identifying AI use cases, deploying solutions at scale, improving operational efficiency, strengthening risk management, and integrating AI capabilities with existing technology systems. The Deputy General Managers will focus on risk and operational analytics, AI governance and compliance, data engineering, model application development, and AI operations. The recruitment drive follows a cyberattack on SBI in which 3,897 customer records were reportedly stolen, and the appointments underscore what the article describes as the growing importance of dedicated AI leadership within financial institutions.

stories.Headline: KPMG's Todd Lohr ties wider AI use to client data control
stories.Summary:
KPMG US vice chair and head of client technology and innovation Todd Lohr gave an interview that Anthropic published on November 23, 2026, about AI and client data. In it he tied wider AI deployment to greater control over client data. He spoke about Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and what they could enable for the firm. The interview was not a deployment announcement, and Lohr did not confirm that KPMG has put the safeguards in place. Lohr said KPMG expects the safeguards to help it expand AI into regulated client work while keeping monitoring records in cloud infrastructure it controls.

Anthropic introduced the safeguards, called EFS, on September 1 and said customer rollout would begin in phases later in fall 2026. The design aims to keep monitoring records in a customer's own cloud account, under its encryption keys, access policies and audit logs. That could preserve the activity history needed to detect misuse without the provider retaining the records. Automated flags would go to KPMG's team for review. Lohr is KPMG US vice chair and head of client technology and innovation, and he framed the issue around the firm's responsibility for information belonging to others.

He said much of the data KPMG handles belongs to clients, including those in highly regulated industries. He said any use must respect both clients' wishes and the purposes for which KPMG may use their information. He said, "We're not going to make a trade-off between AI capability and trust. We expect both." He described an approach combining testing, ongoing monitoring, human oversight, governance and independent assurance.

Lohr said automated misuse review would add a layer to KPMG's existing risk processes, with systems continuously evaluating usage and flagging signs of serious misuse for KPMG's team to review. He presented that automation as an extension of KPMG's Trusted AI program, not a replacement for its other controls. Anthropic says EFS is designed to send detected misuse signals directly to customers, without requiring human review by Anthropic employees. Lohr's advice to other business leaders was to adopt and secure AI at the same time, and he argued that waiting is unlikely to be sustainable for most organizations. Claude is integrated into Digital Gateway, the platform that runs KPMG's tax business, which the firm calls Digital Gateway Powered by Claude.

Lohr described this as part of a strategy to put the firm's industry knowledge, including tax and legal expertise, into AI platforms and products. KPMG uses Claude Mythos to identify vulnerabilities across its enterprise, then uses AI to help patch and secure systems. Lohr said the firm has begun building AI-native ways of working in tax and private equity, and has built cybersecurity services using advanced AI. Anthropic says sophisticated misuse can span multiple sessions and accounts, making isolated checks insufficient. The interview leaves open whether KPMG has adopted the safeguards.

Anthropic said customer rollout would begin in phases later in fall 2026. Lohr described what the safeguards could enable but did not confirm a completed KPMG rollout. Zero data retention by the provider therefore does not mean no records exist, according to Anthropic's proposed answer. The architecture is designed to preserve the history needed for automated detection while giving the customer control over storage and management.

stories.Headline: Elastic releases AlertZero AI Workers to investigate security alerts and propose responses
stories.Summary:
Elastic released a technical preview of AlertZero, a set of AI Workers for investigating security alerts and proposing responses with supporting evidence, on November 24, 2026, according to TechGig. The company said the system aims to reduce the time analysts spend gathering context before deciding how to handle an alert. AlertZero is available in Elastic Security 9.6 on Elastic Cloud Serverless, and teams can choose the models and autonomy settings, including whether proposed actions need approval. Model-driven steps can read data but cannot directly change the environment, and the system collects evidence and presents a proposed action for review or execution depending on its permissions. AlertZero groups six Workers into four Watches covering alert triage, threat hunting, detection engineering and endpoint forensics, and the Workers run on schedules or respond to events such as new alerts.

Each Worker uses Elastic Workflows, with deterministic code handling lookups and checks before a model performs classification or diagnosis, and the Alert Triage Worker gathers previous closures for the relevant rule, its purpose and how frequently it fires. A model assesses the evidence and returns a true-positive or false-positive verdict with a confidence score, and the workflow records the verdict and proposes closing false positives meeting the default minimum confidence score of 85 per cent. There are three autonomy levels: Manual requires explicit approval for proposed actions, Assisted lets Rule Tuning and Rule Coverage begin investigations without asking, and Supervised permits a Worker to approve and execute proposals for subsequent review. Manual mode is not an approval gate for every operation, since Workers can tag and annotate alerts or open investigations without preapproval at any level, and approved actions use the analyst's privileges and are recorded as their decision while actions performed without approval use a service account. Workers can pass findings between tasks, so false positives identified during triage can feed rule tuning and reduce repeated investigation of the same noise.

Endpoint Analysis reconstructs an attack timeline and indicators of compromise on the main host and, through Elastic Defend, can propose host isolation or killing and suspending processes, though closing an Endpoint Analysis investigation always requires approval. Teams select models in Feature Settings across Efficient, Balanced and Frontier tiers, switching a model does not change the underlying workflow, and each tier can use an open-weight or self-hosted model. Elastic said it built AlertZero to do that digging so analysts can spend their time on the calls that really need them. The company states prompts will not go to third-party services when every tier points to self-hosted models, and investigations retain evidence, reasoning, and host and user context for follow-up questions through Agent Builder. Elastic expects AlertZero to reach Elastic Cloud Hosted and Self-Managed deployments in version 9.6 in early December.

stories.Headline: FormFactor gains edge over Applied Materials as HBM demand grows
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials and FormFactor are both described by the article as key players in the AI infrastructure market, serving different purposes in the AI value chain, and the piece weighs which stock has the edge as demand for High Bandwidth Memory grows. Applied Materials develops equipment for deposition, etching and inspection across a wide range of semiconductor nodes, while FormFactor provides electrical and optical test and measurement technologies across the semiconductor product lifecycle, from characterization and design debug to qualification and production test. The article says Applied Materials is benefiting from HBM demand as AI computing pushes demand for advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory, with management reporting full utilization at leading-edge DRAM fabs. DRAM's share of Semiconductor Systems revenues climbed to 33% in fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 from 28% a year earlier, and quarterly DRAM revenues reached a record, according to the article. Management identifies leading-edge DRAM as one of the fastest-growing wafer fabrication equipment categories in 2027 and expects its technology positions to support nodal share gains as memory makers increase complexity.

The article says Applied Materials management now expects calendar 2026 advanced packaging revenues to grow about 90% compared with its previous outlook of more than 70%, and reported record revenues in fourth-quarter fiscal 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Applied Materials' fiscal 2027 bottom line is pegged at $18.97, showing year-over-year growth of 26.8%, and estimates have been revised upward in the past seven days. FormFactor's third-quarter 2026 DRAM revenues held near the second-quarter record at $84.9 million despite a shift from HBM to DDR5, and its SmartMatrix technology supports testing of completed HBM4 stacks at speeds above 10 gigabits per second. For the fourth quarter of 2026, FormFactor expects revenues of $285 million, plus or minus $10 million, and non-GAAP earnings of 95 cents per share, plus or minus nine cents. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FormFactor's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings shows year-over-year growth of 100%, and estimates have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

The article reports that in the past year shares of Applied Materials and FormFactor have gained 31.1% and 41.8% respectively, and that Applied Materials trades at a forward 12-month price-to-sales multiple of 5.06X, below its median of 8.73X, while FormFactor trades at 4.51X, below its median of 8.15X. The article concludes that FormFactor appears to have an edge over Applied Materials, supported by stronger share price appreciation, robust HBM4 and next-generation memory testing demand, and expanding opportunities in high-performance computing and advanced packaging. It says FormFactor's SmartMatrix technology and growing customer programs position it to benefit from rising semiconductor test intensity, and that although FormFactor trades above its historical sales multiple, its stronger growth momentum and earnings prospects make it a compelling pick for investors seeking exposure to the expanding HBM market. The article states that Applied Materials carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while FormFactor sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

stories.Headline: Google engineer says agents need scoped identities and sandboxes to limit insider risk
stories.Summary:
Amanda Walker, Google's senior director of engineering for privacy, safety and security, spoke at QCon San Francisco about securing AI agents in production, framing them as an insider-risk problem that operates at machine speed. She said a rogue AI agent is like a rogue human insider but acts with superhuman speed and persistence, so controls must work at machine speed rather than relying on manual log reviews. She recommended explicit principals for agents, the AI equivalent of service accounts, so each agent can be provisioned and logged separately without impersonating anyone. She cautioned that giving an agent raw human credentials is a fast path to production failure.

Scoped OAuth tokens can limit an agent's access in time and scope but are immutable once issued, while credential attenuation, where an orchestrator mints narrower tokens for its subagents, offers more flexibility, such as read-only access to logs. Eclipse Biscuit is a token format that lets holders append restrictions but not remove existing ones without invalidating the signature. For API keys, a proxy can give the agent a short-lived synthetic key and substitute the real key as traffic leaves, protecting it from prompt injection and exfiltration. Walker noted that virtual machines protect the host but not the resources an agent can access, while container sandboxes, ephemeral runtimes and sidecar proxies like Envoy offer finer control over file system and network access.

She said a perfectly isolated compute sandbox is not useful without policies to constrain agent actions, and she highlighted risks from poisoned skills on public marketplaces that steal API keys and cryptocurrency wallets. Snyk research found that over a third of publicly available skills had at least one security flaw. Agents can also cause harm unintentionally, such as one that invoked an emergency break-glass process after reading internal SRE documentation. Walker stated that tagging identities as agents provides auditability for risk decisions, supporting human-only rules like emergency access and agent-only rules like signed releases in regulated environments.

stories.Headline: Agoda reports 64 per cent faster code reviews with its modular monolith framework
stories.Summary:
Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework called Platform in its post-booking API to reduce code coupling and enforce domain boundaries between different parts of the system. The framework organizes code around business domains such as cancellations, rebooking and payments, and it avoids the need to rewrite the existing service from scratch. Agoda reported that the median code review time for changes backed by the framework was 64 per cent shorter than for legacy code. The company also said the time to initial substantive feedback fell by 34 per cent compared with legacy code.

The framework relies on several practices to keep the code organized, including the Data Mapper pattern, which separates repository-specific models from business logic. Typed builders centralize object creation and transformations, and ArchUnit encodes architectural constraints as automated tests in continuous integration pipelines. Those tests fail builds when violations of the constraints occur, so the boundaries are enforced automatically rather than by manual review. Platform is now the default for new modules, and existing functionality is being migrated incrementally.

Agoda is the company responsible for the change, and it reported the 64 per cent and 34 per cent figures itself. The company said the approach shortened code review times without requiring a full service rewrite. The articles do not name any individual who spoke about the work or give any further statements beyond those figures and descriptions. The articles also do not say what happens next beyond the incremental migration of existing functionality to Platform.

stories.Headline: ASE and SPIL prepare to overtake Amkor by 2027 as server CPUs seek alternative packaging solutions
stories.Summary:
ASE and SPIL are expected to overtake Amkor in the market by 2027. This shift is occurring as server central processing units move beyond the CoWoS technology provided by TSMC. The change is driven by a global shortage of advanced packaging capacity for high end chips. TSMC has fully booked its own production lines to prioritize customers who make AI accelerators. The transition requires server CPUs to find alternative packaging solutions outside of the TSMC ecosystem.

This movement is expected to benefit ASE and SPIL as they capture more of the market share. The shift is specifically linked to the evolving needs of server hardware and AI infrastructure. These changes are projected to reach a tipping point by the year 2027. Flora Wang reported these developments from Taipei on November 23, 2026, for the publication DIGITIMES.

The report indicates that the current supply chain constraints are forcing a redistribution of packaging orders. The industry is reacting to the fact that certain production lines are completely full. This environment creates an opening for other packaging providers to grow their business. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Eternal Materials nearly doubles October pretax profit as advanced packaging materials boost earnings
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's Eternal Materials reported a preliminary pretax profit of NT$254 million for October, which represents a 99.31 percent increase compared to the same month last year. This financial result was driven by the fact that advanced packaging materials have started contributing to the company's earnings. October revenue reached NT$4.058 billion, which is a 30.82 percent increase year-on-year despite an 8.47 percent decline from September. The company also noted that pretax earnings per share for the month stood at NT$0.19.

For the first ten months of the year, the company achieved a cumulative pretax profit of NT$2.937 billion, marking a 50.70 percent increase over the previous year. This cumulative performance resulted in a pretax earnings per share of NT$2.4, which is 1.5 times the level seen during the same period last year. The company attributed these gains to adjustments in its product mix and high shipment levels for Precision Equipment and semiconductor advanced packaging materials. However, shipments of dry film photoresist, Specialty Materials, and synthetic resins declined in October due to fewer working days and the National Day holiday in China.

Company representatives stated that shipments of advanced packaging materials are rising steadily and that Precision Equipment has entered a period of intensive customer acceptance. They explained that while order visibility for traditional products is average, demand for semiconductor packaging materials and Precision Equipment remains positive. The company expressed an optimistic view of these markets and expects full-year growth momentum to continue. They further noted that product mix optimization helped to reduce the pressure caused by the rising costs of raw materials.

The company expects fourth quarter revenue to be flat or slightly lower than the third quarter because of seasonal factors affecting traditional materials. Despite this, the firm believes that the contribution from high-end product lines will rise further during the traditional peak season. Eternal Materials intends to reduce its reliance on the cycles of general electronic materials and traditional resins by expanding its semiconductor operations. Future growth will depend on the recovery of demand in China and the stability of raw material prices.

stories.Headline: LinkedIn engineers build view-agnostic analytics for iOS interfaces
stories.Summary:
LinkedIn engineers developed a view-agnostic analytics system for modern iOS user interface architectures, according to senior software engineer Keerthana Reddy Ragi, as reported by TechGig on November 24, 2026. The system addresses challenges that arise when the logical structure of a user interface does not mirror the native UIKit hierarchy. Traditional iOS analytics relies on UIView instances as the unit of measurement, but modern architectures increasingly use flattened layouts and custom rendering systems. In these systems, elements such as cards and sections are represented by virtual nodes that do not materialise as UIViews, and analytics built solely around UIKit can fail to capture impressions for them.

The system introduces a shared MeasurableNode contract that relaxes the requirement for every measurable element to be a UIView, and a MeasurableNode exposes four properties covering identity, geometry, hierarchy and lifecycle. Both traditional UIViews and virtual nodes can participate in the same analytics system, with existing UIKit views continuing to use native UIKit properties and lifecycle hooks while virtual nodes explicitly provide corresponding information to the analytics layer. The attach and detach methods are central to the approach because they let the layout or rendering system notify the analytics system of node lifecycle events. The design enables gradual adoption, allowing teams to modernise parts of the user interface without rewriting existing analytics.

Ragi and her colleagues faced three main challenges during development, including widespread assumptions in existing codebases that everything is a UIView and the need to balance short-term compatibility with long-term correctness. Enforcing the attach and detach discipline at the framework level was another challenge the engineers had to address. The underlying approach is not limited to UIKit and has broader applicability for mixed UIKit and SwiftUI apps or cross-platform layout engines, according to the article. The report does not say when the system was deployed or what happens next.

stories.Headline: SCHMID launches QuantumLine P+ plating platform to fill copper vias in glass core substrates without voids
stories.Summary:
The SCHMID Group launched the QuantumLine P+ plating platform on November 23, 2026. This new system provides panel-level plating for the metallization of through-glass vias in glass core substrates. The company designed the platform to fill copper vias without creating voids. This technology addresses critical challenges for companies moving from pilot lines to mass production. The platform aims to improve electrical performance and reliability for high-performance computing.

The system fills vias at aspect ratios of up to 50:1 with a uniformity of plus or minus six percent. It supports panel sizes of 510 by 515 millimeters and glass thicknesses from 200 to 1500 micrometers. The platform will be available for order starting in December 2026. SCHMID offers sampling and demonstrations at its technology center in Freudenstadt, Germany. The system claims throughput four to five times higher than conventional plating systems.

Chief Executive Officer Christian Schmid stated that glass core substrates are moving toward industrial scale. He said that metallizing through-glass vias is a deciding step for volume production. Schmid noted that the bottom-up process reaches aspect ratios that conformal plating cannot reliably achieve. He claimed that the company now covers the critical process chain for glass cores on a panel level. This integration provides customers a faster path from development to production.

The technology is intended for manufacturers of next-generation AI processors and high-performance computing. These users are affected because seams and voids in vias put long-term reliability at risk. Conventional bridge-fill and conformal plating approaches reach their limits as via aspect ratios increase. Thick copper overburden on panel surfaces also adds cost during the planarization step. The platform helps eliminate these voids to enhance electrical performance.

Glass offers a flat and dimensionally stable core for finer interconnects and larger packages. The QuantumLine P+ complements other SCHMID tools like QuantumLine H+, PlasmaLine, and InfinityLine L+. These existing tools handle TGV formation, seed layer preparation, and chemical-mechanical polishing. In November 2026, the company announced an order for wet-process equipment in South Asia. This order is for the first glass substrate manufacturing facility in that region.

The company will begin taking orders for the new plating platform in December 2026. Thermal cycling tests have already confirmed the reliability of the filled vias. The articles leave open whether the specific technology will limit the potential customer base to niche markets. There is also uncertainty regarding the actual adoption rate of glass core substrates. Future financial performance depends on these risks and the recognition of new orders.

stories.Headline: San Francisco daters weigh AI views and AI agents when choosing partners
stories.Summary:
People in San Francisco are using attitudes toward artificial intelligence as a new criterion for choosing romantic partners, according to a recent report. Some individuals now avoid dating anyone who works in the AI industry due to concerns about human relationships and jobs. Others have taken the opposite approach by handing the entire dating process over to AI agents to find matches and book dates. This shift in dating preferences was reported by the technology outlet The Verge and detailed by the Seoul Economic Daily. These trends show that AI is becoming a significant yardstick for private matters like marriage and plans for children.

Irene, a 25-year-old analyst who moved to San Francisco last year, saw users on the Hinge app refuse to date AI users. This condition appeared mostly on profiles of people working in nursing, graphic design, and art. Joseph, a 21-year-old software engineer running a San Francisco startup, uses an AI agent to manage his dating life. His system, managed by a virtual assistant in the Philippines, analyzes profiles and sends messages to get two dates a week. Joseph works 14-hour days and uses the AI to judge matches and put dates on his weekend calendar.

Kyle, a researcher at an AI safety nonprofit in his early 20s, worries about how the technology affects society. He criticized employees at leading AI companies for prioritizing high pay or personal interest over the social consequences of the technology. Kyle stated that values regarding the direction of AI development can carry into a long-term relationship. Brian, who works at an AI company, argued that personality and general approach to life matter more than a job title. Brian also noted that the high salaries in the AI industry can work in his favor when dating.

Women messaging Joseph did not know that the messages they exchanged were written by an AI agent. These women are affected by a lack of authenticity because they believe they are talking to a real human being. Participants at a San Francisco bar matchmaking event cheered when a person introduced a tech worker who was unhappy. Other attendees at that event made jokes by pointing out that their presentation slides were made by people, not AI. Annalise Wolf, a co-founder of the event, noted that tech workers with packed schedules want to meet people in person.

The background involves a growing concern that AI could replace human creative work or threaten existing jobs. This resistance to AI has moved beyond dating apps and into face-to-face settings in the city of San Francisco. Some people believe that simply working at an AI company is a mark against a potential romantic partner. Conversely, some people view the technology as an efficient tool that cuts the time and effort required for dating. Others believe that a job alone should not determine whether a person is worth dating despite social impacts.

The AI agent used by Joseph has learned his mannerisms and speech patterns to write messages as if he were typing. The Verge reports that AI is now influencing how people view technology in their most private personal relationships. The articles leave open whether the lack of authenticity in AI-led dating will lead to more long-term relationship failures. It remains unclear if the backlash against AI workers will continue to grow at in-person social events. The reports do not state if more people will adopt AI agents to manage their romantic lives.

stories.Headline: Appian report finds AI-written apps raise maintenance and security costs for UK enterprises
stories.Summary:
A new report from Appian warns that enterprises using artificial intelligence for software development are running into unexpected costs around maintenance and security for applications the company calls "aloneware." The report was published on November 24, 2026, and reported by TechGig, which said Appian describes these as apps developed using AI that carry significant speed potential. Appian's research found that AI coding tools push time and costs further down the software lifecycle, which can make problems more difficult and expensive to resolve. The report highlights downsides such as generated code that is hard for developers to understand and maintain, limited documentation, complex integrations and awkward dependencies.

Two in three, or 64 per cent, of UK enterprise leaders reported increasing time spent on testing, troubleshooting and deployment, even though actual software development with AI was faster. Four in five, or 79 per cent, of UK enterprise leaders have already allocated at least 10 per cent of their technology innovation budgets to testing, deploying and maintaining non-commercially available software, and two in five, or 43 per cent, allocate at least 20 per cent of these budgets. Three in five leaders reported unexpected post-launch costs associated with security or governance. A further three in five struggle to access relevant technical support when apps do not come from enterprise-grade vendors.

Appian CEO Matt Calkins said the most important applications in enterprises need support, and that if people vibe-code them there will be nobody to turn to when problems occur. Calkins added that using AI to build applications on a commercial platform combines the speed of AI with the reliability of supported technology. He suggested this offers a middle ground for enterprises seeking both ownership and security benefits, according to the report.

stories.Headline: China's state intelligence agency runs a secret campaign to obtain AI chips despite US export controls
stories.Summary:
China's state intelligence agency has conducted a covert campaign for at least two years to bypass semiconductor export controls. This secret operation aims to secure advanced chips that are essential for the development of artificial intelligence technology. Chen Yixin, the minister of state security, is leading this effort through a specialized working team that reports directly to him. The agency is working to obtain high-end semiconductors that have become difficult to acquire due to restrictions from the United States and its allies. The mission requires the intelligence unit to help Chinese companies procure advanced chips and bring them into the country.

This team is also tasked with gathering intelligence on global semiconductor supply chains and the broader industry. These actions follow the late 2022 decision by the U.S. Commerce Department to bar Nvidia from exporting advanced chips directly to China. President Xi Jinping established the Central Science and Technology Commission in 2023 to narrow the computing power gap with the United States. Chen Yixin is responsible for the operation and has described Western technology controls as containment aimed at blocking Chinese development.

In an article for a Communist Party journal in April, he stated that China must resolve chokepoint problems in core technologies. He argued that the nation must secure technology that cannot be obtained through asking, buying, or begging. Chen believes that the struggle against containment is a core mission and a national security challenge rather than a simple economic constraint. These intelligence efforts align with a broader strategy of technological self-reliance pursued by President Xi Jinping.

During a Politburo meeting in January, Xi called for extraordinary measures to secure core technologies in priority fields. He emphasized that problems blocking the development of future industries must be resolved as quickly as possible. The Central Science and Technology Commission serves as the driving force behind the vision for securing technological supremacy. More to follow.
